lessons.title: Algebra readiness and equivalence
lessons.objective: Transform equations while preserving equality and verify solutions.
lessons.teaching: An equation is a balance. Every transformation must preserve the same solution set.
lessons.anchor: Apply the same inverse operation to both sides; never teach “crossing over” as magic.

lessons.title: Factorisation and the zero-product principle
lessons.objective: Factor expressions and explain when a product can be set equal to zero.
lessons.teaching: Factoring rewrites a sum as an equivalent product; the zero-product principle applies only when that product equals zero.
lessons.anchor: Factor first; use AB=0 only when the product is equal to zero.

lessons.title: Quadratic equations by factorisation
lessons.objective: Solve factorable quadratics and verify every root in the original equation.
lessons.teaching: Standard form reveals whether factorisation is efficient and keeps all terms on one side.

lessons.title: Quadratic formula
lessons.objective: Use the quadratic formula accurately when factorisation is unsuitable.
lessons.teaching: The formula is a general solution obtained from completing the square; signs and the denominator belong to one structure.

lessons.title: Choosing a quadratic method and rounding
lessons.objective: Select factorisation or the quadratic formula and report exact or rounded roots appropriately.
lessons.teaching: Method choice is based on structure, not habit. Rounding belongs only in the final line unless instructed otherwise.
lessons.anchor: Factor clean integer structures; use the formula for non-factorable forms.

lessons.title: Surd equations and extraneous roots
lessons.objective: Solve surd equations and reject candidates that fail the original equation.
lessons.teaching: Squaring is not logically reversible without a check because it removes sign information.
lessons.anchor: Isolate radical -> state domain -> square -> solve -> check.

lessons.title: Equations in quadratic form
lessons.objective: Use a substitution such as k=x^n, solve the quadratic in k and back-substitute completely.
lessons.teaching: Repeated algebraic structures can be renamed without changing them; the final answers must return to x.
lessons.anchor: Let k=x^n; solve in k; solve x^n=k with real-domain checks.

lessons.title: Exponential equations and common bases
lessons.objective: Solve exponential equations using exponent laws, equivalent bases and valid substitutions.
lessons.teaching: For a positive base not equal to 1, equal powers have equal exponents. Negative right sides require scrutiny.

lessons.title: Linear simultaneous equations
lessons.objective: Solve two linear equations and interpret the ordered pair as their intersection.
lessons.teaching: A solution must satisfy both equations at the same time; elimination and substitution preserve this shared condition.
lessons.anchor: Eliminate or substitute, then check in both equations.

lessons.title: Non-linear simultaneous equations
lessons.objective: Solve systems where substitution produces a quadratic or rational equation.
lessons.teaching: One relation is used to replace a variable in the other; each resulting root must be paired with its matching second coordinate.
lessons.anchor: Isolate -> substitute -> standard form -> solve -> recover paired values.

lessons.title: Quadratic inequalities
lessons.objective: Solve quadratic inequalities using critical values, sign regions and correct endpoint notation.
lessons.teaching: A quadratic inequality asks where a graph is above, below or on the x-axis—not merely where it equals zero.
lessons.anchor: Find roots -> sign chart/graph -> select intervals -> include endpoints only for <= or >=.

lessons.teaching: The expression under the square root controls whether the quadratic formula produces two, one or no real values.
lessons.anchor: Delta=b^2-4ac: >0 two real; =0 repeated; <0 no real roots.

lessons.title: Algebraic fractions and restrictions
lessons.objective: Simplify and solve rational expressions while preserving excluded values.
lessons.teaching: Cancellation removes a factor from an expression, but it does not restore a value that made the original denominator zero.
lessons.anchor: State restrictions before multiplying or cancelling.

lessons.title: Algebraic proof and reasoning
lessons.objective: Build concise algebraic arguments using definitions, parity, inequalities and identities.
lessons.teaching: A proof explains why a statement holds for every allowed value; checking one example is evidence, not proof.
lessons.anchor: Define a general integer or non-negative square, transform logically, conclude.

whiteboards.prompt: Show that n(n+1) is even for integer n.
whiteboards.answer: Consecutive integers: one is even, so the product is even.

whiteboards.prompt: Show that the square of an odd integer is odd.
Show that n^2+n+2 is even for integer n.
whiteboards.answer: n(n+1) is even and adding 2 preserves evenness.

whiteboards.prompt: Explain why 2^m cannot equal a negative number for real m.
whiteboards.answer: A positive base raised to a real power is positive.

whiteboards.prompt: Prove the product of two consecutive even integers is divisible by 8.
whiteboards.answer: Let them be 2k and 2(k+1); product=4k(k+1), and k(k+1) is even.

whiteboards.prompt: Prove if x+y is odd, one of x,y is even and the other odd.
whiteboards.answer: Same parity sums are even; therefore parities differ.

whiteboards.prompt: Explain why squaring an equation can introduce an extraneous root.
whiteboards.answer: Squaring removes sign information; A^2=B^2 allows A=±B.

lessons.title: Contextual modelling
lessons.objective: Translate a context into equations, solve, apply restrictions and interpret the answer.
lessons.teaching: A mathematical root is not automatically a valid contextual answer. Units, sign, domain and meaning decide validity.
lessons.anchor: Define variable -> model -> solve -> reject invalid values -> answer in context.
